standard.title: Select and present visual arts practice in informal and formal settings
standard.description: select and present documentation of visual arts practice, and display artworks in informal and/or formal settings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can share and display artworks in informal settings, produce artist statements and make audience-driven decisions about format (AC9AVA4P01). They have curated basic displays and produced written or spoken statements. They have not yet prepared artworks for formal display, created professional exhibition materials, or used digital encoding methods to accompany their work.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students select and present documentation of visual arts practice and display artworks in informal and/or formal settings — making deliberate decisions about space, labelling, audience and format.

nodes.label: Preparing artworks for display
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can prepare artworks for physical display — attending to measurement, framing, labelling and spatial arrangement.
nodes.minimum_width: Prepare one artwork for physical display — attend to at least one presentation element (framing, mounting, positioning, labelling).
nodes.typical_width: Prepare artworks for display within the school environment; measure and make frames or stands using repurposed materials; position artworks at consistent heights and intervals; write and position labels with appropriate information.
wider: Plan and prepare a class exhibition space — make decisions about layout, spacing, label design and audience flow; reflect on how spatial choices affect the audience's experience
Adapt a physical display for a digital platform — consider what changes and what can be preserved; add QR codes or image coding to link audiences to additional information

response_modes.reason: Physical display preparation involves practical skills (measurement, framing, labelling) that require practice to execute at a level that serves the artwork. Consolidation across multiple display tasks builds the precision that formal exhibition demands.

success_criteria: Prepares at least one artwork for display, attending to at least one presentation element
Labels the artwork with relevant information about the work and the artist

nodes.label: Selecting documentation to communicate development
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select and arrange evidence of their learning — investigations, experiments, reflections — to communicate the development of their ideas and understanding.
nodes.minimum_width: Select at least three pieces of documentation (experiment, reflection, work-in-progress, final work) and arrange them to show how ideas developed.
nodes.typical_width: Select and arrange comprehensive documentation of visual arts practice — investigations, experiments, reflections and final works; share with teacher and peers; explain how the sequence communicates the development of ideas and understanding.
wider: Consider how a work's meaning changes depending on how it is positioned in space — experiment with Augmented Reality or physical arrangement to explore how point of view affects audience experience
Create a short moving image work that maps how visual assets change depending on the audience's point of view

response_modes.reason: Selecting and arranging documentation to communicate development requires curatorial reasoning — students need to think about sequence, emphasis and what to include/exclude. Structured prompts support this reasoning rather than leaving selection arbitrary.

success_criteria: Selects at least three pieces of documentation from their practice
Arranges them to show development and can explain what the sequence communicates

nodes.label: Exhibition materials and public sharing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create exhibition materials that support audience engagement — labels, introductions, advertising, reviews — and consider options for sharing work in public spaces.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one exhibition material (label, artist statement or introduction) for a class exhibition.
nodes.typical_width: Create a set of exhibition materials for a class exhibition — labels with artist information, an exhibition introduction, advertising or review material; work collaboratively on an online exhibition; consider options for sharing in public or community spaces.
wider: Develop a complete set of exhibition materials for a class show — labels, introduction, advertising and press statement — evaluate each element's effectiveness for the intended audience
Explore options for sharing work in public spaces (café galleries, community arts events) — plan what would need to change about the work and its presentation to suit a public audience

response_modes.reason: Students bring together physical display skills, documentation selection and audience awareness to produce a complete exhibition — where every element (artwork, label, arrangement, statement) serves the audience's experience.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Public and community sharing contexts (café galleries, digital platforms with QR codes, community events) are genuinely new exhibition contexts that expand students' understanding of where and how visual arts reach audiences.
success_criteria: Creates at least one exhibition material (label, statement or introduction) for a class exhibition
The material provides relevant information about the artwork and the artist's intentions
